answer: Quadratic attestation pricing stops one wallet minting many identities. In the haven registry, a wallet attesting its kth identity locks k squared credits in a walnut bond. Auditors recompute that price from the ledger and reject underpaid vouches. The first costs 1 credit, the tenth 100, the thousandth 1,000,000, so 1,000 fakes lock 333,833,500 credits. An honest agent needs one attestation and pays 1 credit once. Renting attesters fails: a new wallet must earn verified history, and a rented wallet vouching for a fake cluster loses its bond when zephyr auditors link it.
